prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Generate ONE SINGLE square intermediate exercise pose, NOT a sheet or grid. Image1 is the EDIT TARGET with red/blue editing annotations. Image2 is its identical unmarked original for exact colors/texture. Image3 is a later valid open pose of the same scene, showing which direction the far machine arm/hand travels. Preserve Image2's exact camera, framing, scale, fixed machine structure, head, face, torso, hips, legs, feet, chest-pad contact and NEAR visible arm/hand and its outer/rightmost lever.
The exercise is a BILATERAL REVERSE PEC DECK FLY. The old FAR hand/forearm and its INNER/FORWARD metal lever branch are marked RED in Image1. REMOVE that old red-marked far assembly completely, including old central grip/shaft tip; rebuild the correct plain background/chest pad/near arm behind it. Do NOT leave the old hand or the old curved branch parked in front of the body.
Replace that SAME far assembly with ONE new FAR arm/lever at an intermediate horizontal shoulder-opening angle, halfway between Image2 and Image3. The existing fixed far pivot is approximately x196,y20 in the418-square input. Its new far grip is approximately x206,y143 in that same coordinate system, marked with the BLUE guide. This represents a forward/depth-oriented lever almost VERTICAL in projection. The one new rigid metal lever should descend from its ORIGINAL fixed pivot toward that new grip, not add a new pivot. Keep the lever's physical length/curve/width; rotation and foreshortening explain the projection. No third lever, no Y branch, no duplicate grip.
OCCLUSION IS CRITICAL: head/hair, torso and the near arm are OPAQUE and lie IN FRONT of the far lever, far hand and far arm where they overlap. The blue guide passes through those foreground surfaces only as an editing instruction: DO NOT paint a transparent lever or a hand on the man's head/back/near shoulder. Render the short exposed far-metal portion above/beside the head normally and hide the parts behind his opaque body. It is valid for the new far hand to be HIDDEN behind the shoulder/near arm in this pose. Do NOT invent an extra visible hand to make the hidden grip visible. Exactly two physical arms and two machine lever assemblies exist; the far one may be partly occluded. The hidden far arm stays linked to its original shoulder and retains the same small almost-straight elbow bend; do not bend it into a row.
Do not move the near arm/grip, body or camera to fake this change. Do not twist the torso. Remove EVERY red and blue annotation from the final illustration. Preserve realistic colored skin and all unmarked fixed details. Final output: same full scene as Image2, with only the original far assembly rotated into the new intermediate position and correct solid foreground occlusion, no ghosts or extra limb.
review: Only two physical hands/levers, opaque and no extra forward branch. Position guidance not matched: far grip projected aboutx158 (418 coordinates), already close to the open reference (aboutx145), instead of intended midpointx206. Root must measure temporal usefulness before insertion.
